text:
SacctParsable2 now classifies each row as Record / NotAnAllocation / Malformed. Step rows, grouped array summaries and unrequested jobs are skipped as before; an unreadable row (wrong field count, unparseable JobID, unparseable ExitCode) makes the whole response Left(Diagnostics) naming the offending row text. A requested job can no longer land in AccountingBatch.missing because we failed to read its record.

Also split rows with split("|", 4): Reason is the final --format field, so a reason containing '|' is now one readable row instead of a spurious malformed row -- removing the most likely false positive of the stricter rule.

Rationale for failing the whole response rather than partial success: sacct output is machine generated against a fixed --format, so an unreadable row means our format understanding is wrong and every row is suspect. Partial success naming the bad rows is the better end state but needs an owned AccountingBatch codec first (the current one is circe-derived), so it is deferred to P6f.12/P6f.30.

Evidence: rewrote the fixture test to assert Left with invalid-accounting-exit-code + invalid-accounting-row and that the diagnostic names row 9100_4; added a well-formed-rows test that still isolates summaries/steps/unrelated jobs and still reports genuinely absent 9100_4 as missing; added a reason-with-pipe test. Updated the pre-existing test that asserted Right(Vector.empty) for an unreadable exit code -- that assertion encoded the defect. cli 27/27, local 24/24, agent 11/11, ssh 23/23.
